component.name: PeriHub
component.summary: Configure gaming keyboards and mice without the vendors' apps

description.p: PeriHub configures SteelSeries, Logitech and Corsair keyboards and mice without SteelSeries GG, Logitech G HUB or Corsair iCUE. It has no account and no telemetry, and it never touches firmware.

ul.li: SteelSeries Apex 3 TKL: lighting with reactive effects, brightness and key remapping
Logitech G mice with onboard memory: profiles, DPI, polling rate, buttons, lighting and macros, saved in the mouse
Logitech devices on a Bolt or Unifying receiver: battery, and DPI as an experimental setting
Corsair mice and keyboards: firmware, polling rate and DPI, with experimental lighting
App profiles that switch lighting and mouse profile with the game in focus, and software macros
A backup before every write to a device

description.p: Untested devices are only read until someone confirms them: each device page offers a test report.
PeriHub needs a udev rule to reach the devices, which a Flatpak cannot install by itself. The project page gives the one-line command to install it.

screenshot.caption: DPI levels and polling rate of a Logitech mouse
Buttons and macros of a Logitech mouse

description.p: The older Logitech G mice whose software Logitech removed: the G500s and G700s are read and their DPI in use can be changed, the G9, G9x, G500 and G700 are read. Nobody has tried them yet, and PeriHub never writes their memory.

23 more mice, among them Glorious, Roccat, Pulsar, Lamzu, Cooler Master, EVGA and the Logitech G600, and keyboards with QMK or Vial firmware. Nobody has tried them yet: their settings can be changed at your own risk. The sidebar lists only the devices that are there, a page helps ask for a new one, and each zone of the mouse lighting can keep its own effect.

129 mice of three more brands, ASUS ROG and TUF, SteelSeries and Razer, recognized from the published documentation of their protocols. Nobody has tried them yet: their settings can be changed at your own risk.
First version as a Flatpak. Inside it, autostart goes through the desktop's Background portal, and the optional udev rules come with the commands to run.
Logitech mice are supported by the format of their memory instead of by model, and the devices on a Bolt or Unifying receiver get a page of their own, with their DPI as a first experimental setting.
The Logi Bolt receiver is recognized, a first step for the MX Master 3S.
The Logitech G502 X Wireless is supported.
